answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond, released only after unrelated peers countersign its work over several epochs. A newcomer starts on an island of trust: it may transact, but its attestations carry no weight until its record crosses a bridge of original contributions — graded work, completed trades, a clean history — that a copy cannot fake cheaply. At its nadir, a fresh identity is cheap to create but worthless to wield, so farming shells costs bonds and effort without buying influence, while one honest identity compounds earned standing.
